title: Research memo on lease notice rules
brief: Prepare a concise legal research memo on notice requirements for a commercial lease dispute.

delegate.scenario: A paralegal at fictional Northstar Legal Group is assembling research for an attorney advising a small-business client in a commercial lease dispute in Franklin, a fictional U.S. state. The attorney will use the memo to prepare for a client call on June 12, 2026, and needs relevant authority, practical takeaways, and any research issues that require confirmation.
delegate.inputs:
Research packet for the Alder Street lease matter. Please organize the points for attorney review.

Client: Alder Street Books LLC, a tenant in Franklin. The lease requires written notice before the landlord may terminate for a nonpayment default. The attorney wants to know whether email notice can satisfy the lease and what cure period applies.

Franklin Code § 44-218, as copied in the research folder: "A commercial tenant shall receive at least 10 calendar days after written notice to cure a monetary default." The folder cover sheet says this section took effect 01/01/2024; the legislative-history summary says it took effect 07/01/2024.

In Reed v. Harbor Properties, 81 Franklin App. 206 (2023), the court held that an email could qualify as written notice where the lease expressly permitted email service. The opinion also says the lease's cure period controls if it exceeds the statutory minimum.

Lease excerpt: "Notices may be delivered by personal delivery, certified mail, or email to the addresses listed in this agreement." The docket calendar lists the client call for 06/12/2026. The attorney's email says the client call is scheduled for 06/13/2026.
delegate.goal: Give the attorney a reliable, clearly sourced overview while distinguishing verified law from points that need confirmation.

criteria.text: States that the memo is for the attorney advising the tenant in a Franklin commercial lease dispute.
Separates the relevant legal rules, case analysis, and application to the lease.
Uses only the supplied research and flags missing authority or facts instead of inventing them.
Provides a concise memo with headings and citations for each legal proposition.
Checks jurisdiction, authority, dates, and procedural details, and identifies conflicts for attorney review.

traps.description: The research folder cover sheet and legislative-history summary give different effective dates for Franklin Code § 44-218.
The docket calendar and attorney email give different dates for the client call.

delegate.exemplar: Prepare a concise legal research memo for the attorney advising Alder Street Books LLC in its Franklin commercial lease dispute. Use clear headings for the governing law, case analysis, application to the lease, and open questions; cite the supplied authorities and do not add unsupported law or facts. Explain the practical implications of the notice language and cure-period rule. Check jurisdiction, citations, dates, and procedural details against the packet, and list any conflicts or items needing verification before the attorney relies on them.
